name: crates publish
description: |
  Publish one workspace crate to crates.io. A version already in the sparse
  index is skipped, and a rate limit or a dependency still missing from the
  index is retried after a wait.
inputs:
  crate:
    description: Crate to publish
    required: true
  token:
    description: crates.io token
    required: true
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CRATE: ${{ inputs.crate }}
        RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.token }}
      run: bash "${GITHUB_ACTION_PATH}/run.sh"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

crate="${CRATE:?CRATE required}"
tag="${RELEASE_TAG:?RELEASE_TAG required}"
: "${CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN:?CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN required}"
export CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN
# crates.io refills its new-crate allowance about once per ten minutes.
retry_wait="${RETRY_WAIT:-630}"
propagation_wait="${PROPAGATION_WAIT:-30}"
max_retries="${MAX_RETRIES:-8}"

version="$(cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 \
	| jq -r --arg name "${crate}" '.packages[] | select(.name == $name) | .version')"
if [[ -z "${version}" ]]; then
	echo "::error::the workspace has no crate ${crate}"
	exit 1
fi
if [[ "${tag}" != "v${version}" ]]; then
	echo "::error::tag ${tag} does not match ${crate} ${version}"
	exit 1
fi

index_path() {
	local name="${1,,}"
	case "${#name}" in
		1) echo "1/${name}" ;;
		2) echo "2/${name}" ;;
		3) echo "3/${name:0:1}/${name}" ;;
		*) echo "${name:0:2}/${name:2:2}/${name}" ;;
	esac
}

published() {
	local body
	body="$(curl --fail --silent --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 \
		"https://index.crates.io/$(index_path "${crate}")")" || return 1
	jq -e --arg v "${version}" 'select(.vers == $v)' <<<"${body}" >/dev/null
}

if published; then
	echo "skip ${crate}@${version}: already on crates.io"
	exit 0
fi

attempt=0
while true; do
	attempt=$((attempt + 1))
	status=0
	output="$(cargo publish -p "${crate}" --locked 2>&1)" || status=$?
	printf '%s\n' "${output}"
	if ((status == 0)); then
		echo "published ${crate}@${version}"
		exit 0
	fi
	if grep -Eq 'is already uploaded|already exists on crates\.io index' <<<"${output}"; then
		echo "skip ${crate}@${version}: already published"
		exit 0
	fi
	if grep -Eq 'status 429 Too Many Requests' <<<"${output}"; then
		wait="${retry_wait}"
		reason="rate limited"
	elif grep -Eq 'no matching package named|failed to select a version for the requirement' <<<"${output}"; then
		wait="${propagation_wait}"
		reason="a dependency is not in the index yet"
	else
		echo "::error::publishing ${crate}@${version} failed"
		exit 1
	fi
	if ((attempt >= max_retries)); then
		echo "::error::${crate}@${version}: ${reason} after ${max_retries} attempts"
		exit 1
	fi
	echo "${crate}@${version}: ${reason} (attempt ${attempt}/${max_retries}); waiting ${wait}s"
	sleep "${wait}"
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -r -- "${work}"' EXIT
mkdir "${work}/bin"

cat >"${work}/bin/cargo" <<'CARGO'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
case "$1" in
	metadata)
		printf '{"packages":[{"name":"%s","version":"1.2.3"}]}\n' "${STUB_CRATE:-actup-core}"
		;;
	publish)
		echo "$*" >>"${CALL_LOG}"
		answer="$(head -n 1 "${PLAN}")"
		sed -i 1d "${PLAN}"
		case "${answer}" in
			ok) echo "Uploaded actup-core v1.2.3" ;;
			429) echo "error: the remote server responded with an error (status 429 Too Many Requests)"; exit 101 ;;
			missing) echo "error: no matching package named \`actup-core\` found"; exit 101 ;;
			unselected) echo "error: failed to select a version for the requirement \`actup-core = \"^1.2.3\"\`"; exit 101 ;;
			exists) echo "error: crate version \`1.2.3\` is already uploaded"; exit 101 ;;
			indexed) echo "error: crate actup-core@1.2.3 already exists on crates.io index"; exit 101 ;;
			lookalike) echo "Packaged 12 files, 429.1KiB"; echo "error[E0429]: \`self\` imports are only allowed within a { } list"; exit 101 ;;
			*) echo "error: failed to verify package tarball"; exit 101 ;;
		esac
		;;
esac
CARGO

cat >"${work}/bin/curl" <<'CURL'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
url="${*: -1}"
echo "${url}" >>"${CALL_LOG}"
[[ -f "${INDEX}" ]] || exit 22
cat "${INDEX}"
CURL

cat >"${work}/bin/sleep" <<'SLEEP'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "sleep $1" >>"${CALL_LOG}"
SLEEP
chmod +x "${work}/bin/cargo" "${work}/bin/curl" "${work}/bin/sleep"

failures=0
pass() { echo "ok - $1"; }
fail() {
	echo "not ok - $1"
	failures=$((failures + 1))
}

publish() {
	local plan="$1" index="$2"
	shift 2
	printf '%s' "${plan}" | tr ' ' '\n' >"${work}/plan"
	rm -f "${work}/index"
	if [[ -n "${index}" ]]; then
		printf '%s\n' "${index}" >"${work}/index"
	fi
	: >"${work}/calls"
	env PATH="${work}/bin:${PATH}" PLAN="${work}/plan" INDEX="${work}/index" CALL_LOG="${work}/calls" \
		CRATE=actup-core RELEASE_TAG=v1.2.3 CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=t RETRY_WAIT=600 PROPAGATION_WAIT=30 MAX_RETRIES=3 \
		"$@" "${here}/run.sh" >"${work}/out" 2>&1
}

calls() { tr '\n' ';' <"${work}/calls"; }

if publish "" '{"name":"actup-core","vers":"1.2.3"}' \
	&& grep -q "skip actup-core@1.2.3: already on crates.io" "${work}/out" \
	&& [[ "$(calls)" == "https://index.crates.io/ac/tu/actup-core;" ]]; then
	pass "a version in the sparse index is skipped"
else
	fail "a version in the sparse index is skipped"
fi

if publish "ok" '{"name":"actup-core","vers":"1.2.2"}' \
	&& grep -q "published actup-core@1.2.3" "${work}/out" \
	&& [[ "$(calls)" == "https://index.crates.io/ac/tu/actup-core;publish -p actup-core --locked;" ]]; then
	pass "a version missing from the index is published"
else
	fail "a version missing from the index is published"
fi

if publish "429 missing unselected ok" "" MAX_RETRIES=4 \
	&& [[ "$(calls)" == "https://index.crates.io/ac/tu/actup-core;publish -p actup-core --locked;sleep 600;publish -p actup-core --locked;sleep 30;publish -p actup-core --locked;sleep 30;publish -p actup-core --locked;" ]]; then
	pass "a rate limit and a missing dependency are retried after their waits"
else
	fail "a rate limit and a missing dependency are retried after their waits"
fi

for answer in exists indexed; do
	if publish "${answer}" "" && grep -q "skip actup-core@1.2.3: already published" "${work}/out"; then
		pass "an upload that lost a race is skipped (${answer})"
	else
		fail "an upload that lost a race is skipped (${answer})"
	fi
done

if ! publish "lookalike ok" "" \
	&& grep -q "publishing actup-core@1.2.3 failed" "${work}/out" \
	&& [[ "$(grep -c '^publish' "${work}/calls")" -eq 1 ]]; then
	pass "a build error that mentions 429 fails at once"
else
	fail "a build error that mentions 429 fails at once"
fi

if ! publish "429 429 429 ok" "" \
	&& grep -q "rate limited after 3 attempts" "${work}/out" \
	&& [[ "$(grep -c '^publish' "${work}/calls")" -eq 3 ]]; then
	pass "retries stop after the attempt limit"
else
	fail "retries stop after the attempt limit"
fi

if ! publish "broken ok" "" \
	&& grep -q "publishing actup-core@1.2.3 failed" "${work}/out" \
	&& [[ "$(grep -c '^publish' "${work}/calls")" -eq 1 ]]; then
	pass "any other publish error fails at once"
else
	fail "any other publish error fails at once"
fi

if ! publish "ok" "" RELEASE_TAG=v9.9.9 \
	&& grep -q "tag v9.9.9 does not match actup-core 1.2.3" "${work}/out" && [[ ! -s "${work}/calls" ]]; then
	pass "a tag for another version fails before any request"
else
	fail "a tag for another version fails before any request"
fi

if ! publish "ok" "" CRATE=actup-nope \
	&& grep -q "the workspace has no crate actup-nope" "${work}/out" && [[ ! -s "${work}/calls" ]]; then
	pass "an unknown crate fails before any request"
else
	fail "an unknown crate fails before any request"
fi

for pair in a:1/a ab:2/ab abc:3/a/abc Ab-Cd:ab/-c/ab-cd; do
	name="${pair%%:*}"
	if publish "" '{"vers":"1.2.3"}' CRATE="${name}" STUB_CRATE="${name}" \
		&& [[ "$(calls)" == "https://index.crates.io/${pair#*:};" ]]; then
		pass "the index path of ${name} is ${pair#*:}"
	else
		fail "the index path of ${name} is ${pair#*:}"
	fi
done

if ((failures > 0)); then
	echo "${failures} failed"
	exit 1
fi
echo "all passed"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

tag="${RELEASE_TAG:?RELEASE_TAG required}"
image="${IMAGE:?IMAGE required}"
output="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT required}"

image_tag="${tag//+/_}"
if [[ ! "${image_tag}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}$ ]]; then
	echo "::error::tag ${tag} gives the invalid image tag ${image_tag}"
	exit 1
fi

version="${tag#v}"
if [[ "${version%%+*}" == *-* ]]; then
	prerelease=true
	dist_tag=next
else
	prerelease=false
	dist_tag=latest
fi

{
	echo "prerelease=${prerelease}"
	echo "dist-tag=${dist_tag}"
	echo "image-tags<<EOF"
	echo "${image}:${image_tag}"
	if [[ "${prerelease}" == false ]]; then
		echo "${image}:latest"
	fi
	echo "EOF"
} >>"${output}"
echo "${tag}: prerelease ${prerelease}, npm dist-tag ${dist_tag}"

set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

trap 'rm -r -- "${work}"' EXIT

	if decide "${tag}" && [[ "$(<"${work}/output")" == "${expected}" ]]; then
		pass "${tag}"
	else
		fail "${tag}"
		cat "${work}/out" "${work}/output"
	fi
}

image-tags<<EOF

	&& grep -q "::error::tag v1.0.0-é gives the invalid image tag" "${work}/out" \

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - run: rustup toolchain install
      - parallel:
          - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
          - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
          - &wasmPack
            name: Install wasm-pack
            uses: taiki-e/install-action@8cca0918f8471c33515202b73f56ab27f2bed283 # v2.87.29
            with: { tool: wasm-pack@0.15.0 }
      - name: Zed — clippy
        working-directory: extensions/zed
        run: cargo clippy --target wasm32-wasip2 -- -Dwarnings
      - name: actup-wasm — install
        working-directory: &pkgWasm packages/actup-wasm
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: actup-wasm — build (regenerates tsify-derived `.d.ts` from current Rust)
        working-directory: *pkgWasm
        run: bun run build
      - name: VSCode — install
        working-directory: &extVscode extensions/vscode
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: VSCode — lint + typecheck (against fresh wasm types)
        working-directory: *extVscode
        run: bun run --sequential lint typecheck
      - name: VSCode — test
        working-directory: *extVscode
        run: bun run test

  wasm:
    name: WASM
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - run: rustup toolchain install
      - parallel:
          - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
          - name: Clippy (wasm32)
            run: cargo clippy -p actup-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -Dwarnings
          - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
          - *wasmPack
      - name: Install npm deps
        working-directory: &pkgWasm packages/actup-wasm
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Build
        working-directory: *pkgWasm
        run: bun run build
      - name: Typecheck
        working-directory: *pkgWasm
        run: bun run typecheck
      - name: Test
        working-directory: *pkgWasm
        run: bun run test
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
      - name: Crate node tests
        run: just wasm-node-test

  action:
    name: Action and example scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: kjanat/actionlint@v1
      - run: shellcheck action/*.sh examples/*.sh .github/actions/crates-publish/*.sh .github/actions/release-version/*.sh
      - run: ./action/test.sh
      - run: ./examples/pin.test.sh
      - run: ./.github/actions/crates-publish/test.sh
      - run: sudo locale-gen en_US.UTF-8
      - run: ./.github/actions/release-version/test.sh

  self-check:
    name: Self-check pins
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - run: rustup toolchain install
      - parallel:
          - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
          - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
      - run: just self-check-pins
        env: { GITHUB_TOKEN: "${{ github.token }}" }

  # Final status check for branch protection
  ci-success:
    name: CI Success
    if: always()
    needs: [fmt, clippy, test, test-platforms, doc, machete, deny, msrv, coverage, check-extensions, wasm, action, self-check]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check all jobs passed
        env:
          FMT: ${{ needs.fmt.result }}
          CLIPPY: ${{ needs.clippy.result }}
          TEST: ${{ needs.test.result }}
          TEST_PLATFORMS: ${{ needs.test-platforms.result }}
          DOC: ${{ needs.doc.result }}
          MACHETE: ${{ needs.machete.result }}
          DENY: ${{ needs.deny.result }}
          MSRV: ${{ needs.msrv.result }}
          COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage.result }}
          CHECK_EXTENSIONS: ${{ needs.check-extensions.result }}
          WASM: ${{ needs.wasm.result }}
          ACTION: ${{ needs.action.result }}
          SELF_CHECK: ${{ needs.self-check.result }}
        run: if [[ "${FMT}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${CLIPPY}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${TEST}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${TEST_PLATFORMS}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${DOC}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${MACHETE}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${DENY}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${MSRV}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${COVERAGE}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${CHECK_EXTENSIONS}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${WASM}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${ACTION}" != "success" ]] ||
          [[ "${SELF_CHECK}" != "success" ]];
          then { echo "One or more jobs failed"; exit 1; };
          fi; echo "All jobs passed"

name: Release files
on:
  push: { branches: [master] }
  pull_request:
permissions: { contents: read }
jobs:
  docs:
    name: Release archive documents exist
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: { persist-credentials: false }

      - name: Check every file the Package step copies
        run: |
          docs="$(yq '.jobs.build.steps[] | select(.name == "Package") | .env.RELEASE_DOCS' .github/workflows/release.yml)"
          if [[ -z "${docs}" || "${docs}" == null ]]; then
            echo "::error file=.github/workflows/release.yml::the Package step sets no RELEASE_DOCS"
            exit 1
          fi
          missing=0
          for file in ${docs}; do
            if [[ ! -f "${file}" ]]; then
              echo "::error::release.yml copies ${file}, which the repository lacks"
              missing=1
            fi
          done
          exit "${missing}"

  crate-licences:
    name: Published crates carry their licence files
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: { persist-credentials: false }

      - run: rustup toolchain install

      - name: Check the licence files of every crate the release publishes
        run: |
          crates="$(yq '.jobs.crates-verify.steps[] | select(.id == "package") | .env.CRATES' .github/workflows/release.yml)"
          if [[ -z "${crates}" || "${crates}" == null ]]; then
            echo "::error file=.github/workflows/release.yml::the crates-verify package step sets no CRATES"
            exit 1
          fi
          metadata="$(cargo metadata --no-deps --locked --format-version 1)"
          missing=0
          for crate in ${crates}; do
            license="$(jq -r --arg name "${crate}" '.packages[] | select(.name == $name) | .license // ""' <<<"${metadata}")"
            if [[ -z "${license}" ]]; then
              echo "::error::${crate} declares no license"
              missing=1
              continue
            fi
            manifest="$(jq -r --arg name "${crate}" '.packages[] | select(.name == $name) | .manifest_path' <<<"${metadata}")"
            dir="$(dirname "${manifest}")"
            listing="$(cargo package --list --locked -p "${crate}")"
            for id in ${license//[()]/ }; do
              case "${id}" in
                OR | AND) continue ;;
                MIT) file=LICENSE-MIT ;;
                Apache-2.0) file=LICENSE-APACHE ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::${crate} declares ${id}, which this check cannot map to a file"
                  missing=1
                  continue
                  ;;
              esac
              if ! grep -qxF "${file}" <<<"${listing}"; then
                echo "::error::${crate} declares ${id}, and its package lacks ${file}"
                missing=1
              elif ! cmp "${dir}/${file}" "${file}"; then
                echo "::error::${crate} packs a ${file} that differs from the repository's ${file}"
                missing=1
              fi
            done
          done
          exit "${missing}"

  image-licences:
    name: Container image carries the licence files
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: { persist-credentials: false }

      - name: Build the image around a stub binary and compare its licence files
        run: |
          mkdir -p docker/amd64
          printf 'stub\n' >docker/amd64/actup
          docker build --platform linux/amd64 --tag actup-licences .
          container="$(docker create actup-licences)"
          missing=0
          for file in LICENSE-MIT LICENSE-APACHE; do
            if ! docker cp "${container}:/usr/share/doc/actup/${file}" "${RUNNER_TEMP}/${file}"; then
              echo "::error file=Dockerfile::the image lacks /usr/share/doc/actup/${file}"
              missing=1
            elif ! cmp "${file}" "${RUNNER_TEMP}/${file}"; then
              echo "::error file=Dockerfile::/usr/share/doc/actup/${file} differs from ${file}"
              missing=1
            fi
          done
          docker rm "${container}"
          exit "${missing}"
files..github/workflows/release.yml:
name: Release
on: { push: { tags: ["v*"] } }
concurrency: { group: release, cancel-in-progress: false }
permissions: { contents: read }
env: { CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always }
jobs:
  build:
    name: Build (${{ matrix.target }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        cross: [false]
        archive: [.tar.gz]
        package: [actup]
        ext: [""]
        include:
          # Linux
          - { os: ubuntu-latest, target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu }
          - { os: ubuntu-latest, target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl }
          - { os: ubuntu-latest, target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, cross: true }
          - { os: ubuntu-latest, target: aarch64-unknown-linux-musl, cross: true }
          # macOS
          - { os: macos-15-intel, target: x86_64-apple-darwin }
          - { os: macos-latest, target: aarch64-apple-darwin }
          # Windows
          - { os: windows-latest, target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, archive: .zip, ext: .exe }
          - { os: windows-11-arm, target: aarch64-pc-windows-msvc, archive: .zip, ext: .exe }

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Install Rust
        shell: bash
        run: rustup toolchain install && rustup target add "${TARGET}"
        env: { TARGET: "${{ matrix.target }}" }

      - name: Install musl tools
        if: contains(matrix.target, 'musl')
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y musl-tools

      - name: Install cross
        if: matrix.cross
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@8cca0918f8471c33515202b73f56ab27f2bed283 # v2.87.29
        with:
          tool: cross

      - name: Build (cross)
        if: matrix.cross
        shell: bash
        run: cross build --release --target "${TARGET}" -p "${PACKAGE}"
        env: { TARGET: "${{ matrix.target }}", PACKAGE: "${{ matrix.package }}" }

      - name: Build (native)
        if: "!matrix.cross"
        shell: bash
        run: cargo build --release --target "${TARGET}" -p "${PACKAGE}"
        env: { TARGET: "${{ matrix.target }}", PACKAGE: "${{ matrix.package }}" }

      - name: Package
        shell: bash
        env:
          REF_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          ARCHIVE: ${{ matrix.archive }}
          PACKAGE: ${{ matrix.package }}
          EXT: ${{ matrix.ext }}
          RELEASE_DOCS: README.md LICENSE-MIT LICENSE-APACHE
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          cp "target/${TARGET}/release/${PACKAGE}${EXT}" dist/
          read -ra docs <<<"${RELEASE_DOCS}"
          cp "${docs[@]}" dist/
          if [[ "${ARCHIVE}" == ".zip" ]]; then
            cd dist && 7z a "../${PACKAGE}-${REF_NAME}-${TARGET}${ARCHIVE}" ./*
          else
            tar -czvf "${PACKAGE}-${REF_NAME}-${TARGET}${ARCHIVE}" -C dist .
          fi

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.package }}-${{ matrix.target }}
          path: ${{ matrix.package }}-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ matrix.target }}${{ matrix.archive }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1
          compression-level: 9

  checksums:
    name: Generate checksums
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: actup-*
          path: artifacts
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Generate SHA256 checksums
        working-directory: artifacts
        run: sha256sum actup-* | tee SHA256SUMS.txt

      - name: Attest release checksums
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with: { subject-path: artifacts/SHA256SUMS.txt }

      - name: Upload checksums
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: checksums
          path: artifacts/SHA256SUMS.txt

  version:
    name: Release version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      prerelease: ${{ steps.version.outputs.prerelease }}
      dist-tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.dist-tag }}
      image-tags: ${{ steps.version.outputs.image-tags }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: { persist-credentials: false }

      - id: version
        uses: $/.github/actions/release-version
        with: { image: ghcr.io/kjanat/actup }

  release:
    name: Create Release
    needs: [build, checksums, crates-verify, npm-verify, version]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with: { pattern: actup-*, path: artifacts, merge-multiple: true }

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with: { name: checksums, path: artifacts }

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@efb35369e0ad2afab669f228072c1b0d510eae64 # v3.0.3
        with:
          files: artifacts/*
          generate_release_notes: true
          draft: false
          prerelease: ${{ needs.version.outputs.prerelease == 'true' }}
        env: { GITHUB_TOKEN: "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" }

  image:
    name: Publish container image
    needs: [release, version]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: actup-*-unknown-linux-musl
          path: artifacts
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Unpack musl binaries
        env: { REF_NAME: "${{ github.ref_name }}" }
        run: |
          for pair in amd64:x86_64 arm64:aarch64; do
            arch="${pair%%:*}"
            mkdir -p "docker/${arch}"
            tar -xzf "artifacts/actup-${REF_NAME}-${pair#*:}-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" -C "docker/${arch}" ./actup
          done

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1

      - uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          push: true
          tags: ${{ needs.version.outputs.image-tags }}
          build-args: |
            ACTUP_VERSION=${{ github.ref_name }}
            ACTUP_REVISION=${{ github.sha }}

  crates-verify:
    name: Verify crates.io packages
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      crates: ${{ steps.package.outputs.crates }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: { persist-credentials: false }

      - run: rustup toolchain install

      - name: Check the tag, then package and build every crate in publish order
        id: package
        env:
          CRATES: tree-sitter-github-actions actup-core actup-providers actup-provider-github actup-provider-gitlab actup-provider-gitea actup actup-lsp actup-mcp
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          read -ra crates <<<"${CRATES}"
          crates_json="$(jq -cn '$ARGS.positional' --args "${crates[@]}")"
          echo "crates=${crates_json}" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          metadata="$(cargo metadata --no-deps --locked --format-version 1)"
          mismatched=0
          for crate in "${crates[@]}"; do
            version="$(jq -r --arg name "${crate}" '.packages[] | select(.name == $name) | .version' <<<"${metadata}")"
            if [[ "${TAG}" != "v${version}" ]]; then
              echo "::error::tag ${TAG} does not match ${crate} ${version:-(no such crate)}"
              mismatched=1
            fi
          done
          if ((mismatched)); then
            exit 1
          fi
          args=()
          for crate in "${crates[@]}"; do
            args+=(-p "${crate}")
          done
          cargo package --locked "${args[@]}"

  publish:
    name: Publish ${{ matrix.crate }} to crates.io
    needs: [release, crates-verify]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ !github.event.repository.private }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: crates-io
      url: https://crates.io/crates/${{ matrix.crate }}
    strategy:
      max-parallel: 1
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        crate: ${{ fromJSON(needs.crates-verify.outputs.crates) }}
    env:
      HAS_CRATES_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN != '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: { persist-credentials: false }

      - run: rustup toolchain install

      # Trusted publishing on crates.io requires an existing crate.
      - name: Mint crates.io token
        id: auth
        if: env.HAS_CRATES_TOKEN != 'true'
        uses: rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@3268eb413133e2960fa4ae0e963ca76380c54cd9 # v1.0.6

      - name: Publish
        uses: $/.github/actions/crates-publish
        with:
          crate: ${{ matrix.crate }}
          token: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN || steps.auth.outputs.token }}

  npm-verify:
    name: Verify the npm package
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: { persist-credentials: false }

      - name: Check the tag against the package version
        env: { TAG: "${{ github.ref_name }}" }
        run: |
          version="$(jq -r '.version' packages/actup-wasm/package.json)"
          if [[ "${TAG}" != "v${version}" ]]; then
            echo "::error file=packages/actup-wasm/package.json::tag ${TAG} does not match actup-wasm ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: rustup toolchain install
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
      - name: Install wasm-pack
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@8cca0918f8471c33515202b73f56ab27f2bed283 # v2.87.29
        with:
          tool: wasm-pack@0.15.0
      - name: Install deps
        working-directory: packages/actup-wasm
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Build
        working-directory: packages/actup-wasm
        run: bun run build
      - name: Test
        working-directory: packages/actup-wasm
        run: bun run test
      - name: Pack
        working-directory: packages/actup-wasm
        run: |
          npm pack --dry-run
          mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/npm-package"
          npm pack --pack-destination "${RUNNER_TEMP}/npm-package"
      - name: Check and smoke-test the packed tarball
        working-directory: packages/actup-wasm
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          tarballs=("${RUNNER_TEMP}"/npm-package/*.tgz)
          if ((${#tarballs[@]} != 1)); then
            echo "::error::expected one npm tarball, found ${#tarballs[@]}"
            exit 1
          fi
          listing="$(tar -tzf "${tarballs[0]}")"
          missing=0
          for file in package/dist/index.js package/dist/provider.js package/wasm/actup_wasm_bg.wasm package/LICENSE-MIT package/LICENSE-APACHE; do
            if ! grep -qxF "${file}" <<<"${listing}"; then
              echo "::error::the npm tarball lacks ${file}"
              missing=1
            fi
          done
          if ((missing)); then
            exit 1
          fi
          unpacked="${RUNNER_TEMP}/npm-unpacked"
          mkdir -p "${unpacked}"
          tar -xzf "${tarballs[0]}" -C "${unpacked}"
          mkdir "${unpacked}/package/tests"
          cp tests/node_import.mjs "${unpacked}/package/tests/"
          node "${unpacked}/package/tests/node_import.mjs"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: npm-package
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/npm-package/*.tgz
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  publish-npm:
    name: Publish to npm
    needs: [release, npm-verify, version]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ !github.event.repository.private }}
    environment: npm
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with: { name: npm-package, path: npm-package }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
      - name: Publish
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          tarballs=(./npm-package/*.tgz)
          if ((${#tarballs[@]} != 1)); then
            echo "::error::expected one npm tarball, found ${#tarballs[@]}"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${DIST_TAG}" != latest && "${DIST_TAG}" != next ]]; then
            echo "::error::the version job picked no dist-tag"
            exit 1
          fi
          npm publish "${tarballs[0]}" --provenance --access public --tag "${DIST_TAG}"
        env:
          DIST_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.dist-tag }}
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
files.Cargo.toml:
[workspace]

files.README.md:
![actup — Check. Update. Pin.](branding/banner.svg)

GitHub Actions version manager. CLI + LSP + MCP for checking and updating
`uses:` refs across workflows and composite actions.

## Features

- **Check** workflows for outdated action versions
- **Update** to latest versions (respecting semver policy)
- **Pin** refs to immutable commit SHAs for security
- **Providers**: GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab and Gitea/Forgejo
  ([`docs/providers.md`](docs/providers.md))
- **LSP**: Editor diagnostics and code actions
- **MCP**: stdio server with read tools and dry-runnable mutators confined to
  one root

Local paths (`./`, `../`) and same-repository references (`$/`) are skipped when
checking, updating or pinning versions. This includes actions and reusable
workflows such as `$/.github/actions/setup` and `$/.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Installation

```sh
# From source (requires Rust 1.96+)
cargo install --git https://github.com/kjanat/actup actup
cargo install --git https://github.com/kjanat/actup actup-lsp
cargo install --git https://github.com/kjanat/actup actup-mcp
```

### GitHub Action

The action downloads the release that its ref names, checks the archive against
the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and runs it. Linux runners get the static musl
build.

```yaml
- uses: kjanat/actup@<commit SHA of v1.2.3> # v1.2.3
  with:
    version: v1.2.3 # needed when the ref is a commit SHA
    command: check # check, update, pin or config
    args: --strict # split on whitespace
```

| Input               | Default               | Meaning                                                 |
| ------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `command`           | `check`               | actup subcommand                                        |
| `args`              | `""`                  | Extra arguments after the subcommand                    |
| `working-directory` | `.`                   | Directory to run actup in                               |
| `version`           | `""`                  | Release tag to run when the action ref is not a release |
| `github-token`      | `${{ github.token }}` | Passed to actup as `GITHUB_TOKEN`                       |

A ref that is neither a release tag like `v1.2.3` nor paired with `version`
fails the step. Inside another composite action, `github.action_ref` names that
outer action, and actup then needs `version`. The download always comes from the
`kjanat/actup` releases. Outputs: `exit-code` (see [Exit Codes](#exit-codes))
and `actup-bin`, the path of the verified binary for later steps.

`examples/workflows/` holds a check workflow and a reusable workflow that opens
an update pull request with the `token` secret it receives. After tagging a
release, `just examples-pin <tag>` pins both examples to the tag's commit.

the tag becomes `_` in the image tag, so `v1.0.0+build-5` publishes
`:v1.0.0_build-5`. The image runs actup in `/work` as a non-root user.

# Run as your own user so `update` and `pin` can write your files
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD:/work" -e GITHUB_TOKEN ghcr.io/kjanat/actup:v1.2.3 update
``` -->

## Quick Start

```sh
# Check current directory for outdated actions
actup check

# Check with strict mode (exit 1 if outdated)
actup check --strict

# Exit 1 only for major bumps or floating branch refs
actup check --fail-on major --fail-on floating

# Update all actions to latest versions
actup update

# Pin all actions to their current SHA
actup pin

# Turn `@<sha> # v4` back into `@v4` where the tag is still on that commit
actup pin --unpin

# Preview changes without applying
actup update --dry-run
```

## Commands

| Command       | Description                                    |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `check`       | Scan workflows, report outdated (read-only)    |
| `update`      | Update actions to latest versions              |
| `fix`         | Alias for `update`                             |
| `pin`         | Pin all actions to their current commit SHA    |
| `pin --unpin` | Unpin marked SHA pins back to their tag        |
| `config`      | Show effective configuration                   |
| `cache`       | Manage version cache (`info`, `clear`, `path`) |
| `schema`      | Output JSON schema for config file             |
| `completions` | Generate shell completions                     |

### Output Formats

```sh
actup check --format json  # Machine-readable JSON
actup check --format toml  # TOML format
actup check --format human # Default, colored output
actup check --format table # One aligned row per finding
actup check --format sarif # SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning
```

`--format table` prints the columns `LOCATION` (`file:line`), `ACTION`,
`CURRENT`, `TARGET` (`-` when there is none) and `STATUS` (the JSON status
name). Only `check` accepts `table` and `sarif`; other commands reject them,
also when `ACTUP_FORMAT` sets them.

`--format sarif` writes one result per finding other than up-to-date and ignored
refs, under one rule per status (`actup/outdated`, `actup/floating`,
`actup/unresolvable` and so on). Levels follow the LSP severities: `error` for
an unresolvable ref, `warning` for an outdated or floating ref, and `note` for
pinned and unknown refs, environment errors and same-commit refs. Paths are
percent-encoded URIs relative to the scanned directory, or `file:///` URIs for
absolute paths. A backslash separates segments and a drive letter makes a path
absolute on Windows alone. Columns count UTF-16 code units. Files that could not
be read appear as execution notifications.

`check --github-annotations` also writes one `::error` or `::warning` workflow
command per error or warning finding to stderr, whatever `--format` is.

```yaml
- run: actup check --format sarif --github-annotations > actup.sarif
- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  if: always()
  with: { sarif_file: actup.sarif }
```

`check --fail-on <kind>` exits 1 when a finding of that kind exists. Repeat it
for several kinds. `outdated` covers outdated refs and branch refs to pin,
`major` covers outdated refs whose target is a newer major version, and
`floating` covers floating branch refs and branch refs to pin. `--strict` is
`--fail-on outdated`. Unresolvable refs exit 2 and environment errors exit 3
with or without `--fail-on`.

Human output is coloured only on a terminal. `--color always` and
`--color never` force the choice. Under the default `--color auto`, a non-empty
`NO_COLOR` turns colour off, and a `CLICOLOR_FORCE` other than `0` turns it on
for piped output. `NO_COLOR` wins when both are set.

Human output, LSP messages and `--github-annotations` lines replace control
characters other than tab and line feed, zero-width and bidi control characters,
and the byte order mark with U+FFFD. Human output and LSP messages also replace
line feeds in paths, `uses:` values, refs, versions, reasons and error messages.
JSON output writes DEL as `\u007f` and `##[` as `##\u005b`, and keeps the rest
of the raw text. A GitHub Actions runner splits output into lines at CR and LF,
reads a line that starts with `::` as a workflow command and reads a line that
contains `##[` as a legacy one. Human output, TOML output and logs replace the
first colon of such a line and the `[` of every `##[` with U+FFFD. The runner
then reads only `--github-annotations` lines as workflow commands. Annotations
percent-encode `%`, CR and LF, and also `:` and `,` in the file name.

With `--format json` or `toml`, `check` prints one entry per finding and
`update` and `pin` print a report with `dry_run` and the lists `edited`,
`skipped` and `errors`. Every entry names the file, line, action, owner, repo,
host, provider and `reference` (the ref as found). `host` is the ref's own host,
or the default host for a ref without one. An `edited` entry adds `to` (the ref
written) and `comment` when the edit writes a comment after it. A `skipped`
entry adds `reason`: `ignored` when `scan.ignore` matches the ref, or
`unplaceable`, `overlap` or `out_of_bounds` when the writer cannot edit it. Only
the last three make `update` and `pin` exit 1. When two edits of a file overlap,
every edit of that file is skipped with `overlap` and the file stays unchanged.
An `errors` entry adds `kind` (such as `invalid_ref`, `not_found`,
`rate_limited`, `provider_not_found`, `write`, `changed` or `invalid_edit`) and
`message`. With no workflow files, the report has empty lists and `check` prints
no findings.

A remote `uses:` value without `@`, with an empty ref, or with a ref that is not
a git ref name (such as `o/r@a~1` or `o/r@v1.lock`) reaches no provider. `check`
reports it as unresolvable, `update` and `pin` report it with kind
`invalid_ref`, and all three exit 2. The language server marks it with an error
diagnostic. This holds for a value under `jobs.<id>.uses`,
`jobs.<id>.steps[*].uses` or `runs.steps[*].uses`, including steps nested inside
`parallel:` lists. An invalid value under any other `uses` key, such as a step
input, is skipped.

An unresolvable ref that names no tag can get a suggested tag. A partial version
names the highest tag that completes it (`v4.2` names the highest `v4.2.x`). A
full version names a listed tag of the same version (`4.2.0` names `v4.2.0`),
and gets no suggestion when none exists. Any other ref names the tag within two
edits of it, and the higher version wins a tie (`v4.2.O` names `v4.2.0`). A
partial version that no tag completes takes only full `X.Y.Z` tags within two
edits (`v42.0` names `v4.2.0`, `v7` names nothing). Prerelease tags count only
under `policy.prerelease = true`. `check` prints the suggestion on a `hint:`
line and adds `suggestion` to the JSON and TOML entry. The LSP offers a
`Change to` quick fix that writes the tag in the `policy.pin` style.

`check`, `update` and `pin` read every file first. They then fetch the versions
of each repo that an unignored ref names, once per repo and in one batch through
the version cache, before they report or edit.

While they fetch, they draw a one-line `resolving N repos` counter on stderr
when stderr is a terminal and `--verbose` is off. Piped and redirected runs
print no progress.

`--offline` reads versions only from the cache. A repo missing from the cache,
or cached longer ago than `cache.ttl`, makes its refs environment errors (exit
3), and no command touches the network. `--no-cache` neither reads nor writes
the cache, the same as `cache.enabled = false`. `--refresh` skips cached
versions and writes the freshly fetched ones. A repo that fails to fetch keeps
its cache entry. Only one of the three flags can be given. The quick lookup
`actup owner/repo` uses the cache too.

A cache entry past its TTL stays on disk. When the provider then rate limits the
refresh or the network fails, `check` reports the finding from that entry,
prints `stale (fetched 26h ago, rate limited, resets in 12m)` under it, adds
`stale` with `age_secs`, `reason` (`rate_limited` or `network`) and
`retry_after_secs` (when the provider named a reset) to the JSON and TOML entry,
and exits 3. `update` and `pin` refuse to write from such data, report the ref
with kind `stale` and exit 3. `actup-lsp` appends the same note to the
diagnostic and offers no quick fix and no fix-all edit for it. A REST refresh
sends the stored `ETag`s of the tags, repository and default branch requests,
and an answer of 304 to all three renews the entry without a new listing.

`update` and `pin` write each file to a temp file in its directory, flush it,
give it the mode of the original and rename it over the original. A failed write
leaves the original intact. A write through a symlink replaces the file it
points to, and a leading byte order mark stays. They re-read each file before
writing it. When a line they edit differs from the scan, they leave the file
untouched, report each of its refs with kind `changed` and the message
`edit refused: <path> changed since scan`, and exit 3. They also parse the
edited text before writing it. When it is not valid YAML or holds a different
number of `uses:` values, they leave the file untouched, report each of its refs
with kind `invalid_edit`, and exit 2. A dry run reports the same refusal. The
LSP command `actup-lsp/fixAllInWorkspace` applies both checks and leaves out a
refused file.

## Configuration

Create `actup.toml` or `.actup.toml` in your repo root, or write the user config
(see [Config Discovery](#config-discovery)):

```toml
# Default host for bare owner/repo refs (user or explicit config only)
default_host = "github.com"

[policy]
bump       = "minor"     # patch | minor | major | latest
pin        = "preserve"  # preserve | tag | sha
track      = "keep"      # keep | major | exact
major_tag  = "exact"     # exact | contains
branch     = "warn"      # ignore | warn | update
prerelease = false
archived   = "hint"      # hint | ignore

[pin]
comment = true  # add version labels to SHA pins

[scan]
ignore      = ["my-org/*", "dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.91.0"]
extra_paths = [".gitea/workflows"]                           # user or explicit config only

# Ordered; for each policy key the last matching entry wins.
# Patterns are `[host/]owner/repo[/subpath][@ref]` globs.
[[overrides]]
pattern = "my-org/*"
policy  = { pin = "sha" }

[[overrides]]
pattern = "ghe.example.com/platform/*"
policy  = { bump = "patch", track = "exact" }

# API fallback, used only when a host refuses a git connection
[fetch]
api_mode          = "graphql"  # preferred: "graphql" or "rest"; REST-only providers use REST
max_tags_per_repo = 10         # Tags to fetch per repo (1-255)

# Enterprise GitHub (api_base and token_env: user or explicit config only)
[hosts."ghe.example.com"]
kind      = "github"
api_base  = "https://ghe.example.com/api/v3"
token_env = "GHE_TOKEN"
```

### Action Patterns

`scan.ignore` and `[[overrides]]` patterns read a host with the `uses:` rule.
The first segment is a host when the pattern has at least three segments and
that segment is `localhost`, a dotted DNS name, a DNS name with a `:port`, or a
bracketed IPv6 literal such as `[::1]`. Glob characters count as DNS name
characters, so `*.corp.com/o/*` and `ghe.*/o/r` name hosts. A bracketed IPv6
host matches literally.

Host matching ignores case, and a ref without a host matches as `default_host`.
A pattern without a host matches every host. Owner, repo, subpath and ref match
case-sensitively. `*` stays within one segment and `**` spans segments.

In `uses:` refs, actup lower-cases the host. Owner and repo must match
`[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` and must not be `.` or `..`.

A pattern whose owner or repo holds any other character is an error at config
load. Glob syntax is the exception: `*`, `?` and a `[...]` class, whose members
may also be `!` and `]`. Outside a class, `!` and `]` are errors. So is a host
with a glob port such as `ghe.corp:*`; write the port number.

### Pin Style

`policy.pin` sets how `update`, the LSP quick fixes, fix-all and the wasm
`planUpdates` write an outdated ref. An `[[overrides]]` entry can set it per
action.

| `pin`      | Tag ref `@v4.0.0` | SHA pin `@<old> # v4.0.0` |
| ---------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| `preserve` | `@v4.2.0`         | `@<new> # v4.2.0`         |
| `sha`      | `@<new> # v4.2.0` | `@<new> # v4.2.0`         |
| `tag`      | `@v4.2.0`         | `@v4.2.0`                 |

A comment after the ref whose first word is a label gets the new label and keeps
the note after it: `# v4.0.0 pinned for node16` becomes
`# v4.2.0 pinned for node16`. A label is a version such as `v4.0.0`, the ref
being replaced, or a tag or branch that the fetched refs of the action list. A
SHA pin gets `# <version> <note>`, a tag written over a tag or branch gets
`# <tag> <note>`, and a branch, or a tag written over a SHA pin, gets
`# <note>`. `@main # main keep` moved to `v4.2.0` becomes
`@v4.2.0 # v4.2.0 keep`, and `@<sha> # main keep` re-pinned becomes
`@<new> # v4.2.0 keep`. Any other comment, such as `# lint keep` or
`# TODO fix`, stays as written.

A new `# vX.Y.Z` comment is added only where the line can take it: never next to
another comment, never on a line that holds other `uses:` values or ends inside
a scalar, and never in a plain-text file. The comment goes after the closing
quote and the flow `}` or `]` that close the value, as in
`{ uses: "o/b@<sha>" } # v4.2.0`, and replaces the trailing whitespace of the
line. Other text after the value, such as more flow keys, means no new comment,
but a label comment at the end of the line is still rewritten and keeps its
note. `actup pin` and `branch = "update"` place their `# <ref>` comment the same
way. The CLI, the LSP, the MCP server and the wasm package follow the same rule.

Set `[pin] comment = false` to omit generated labels from SHA edits on all four
surfaces. Replacing a ref removes its recognized label and keeps the note:
`@v4.0.0 # v4.0.0 keep` becomes `@<sha> # keep`. Other comments and closing
quotes stay intact. This setting does not change `policy.pin`, tag updates, or
already-current refs that need no edit. `ACTUP_PIN__COMMENT=false` overrides it.

Action hovers show the action's inputs (description, required flag, and default)
and outputs from `action.yml`, followed by its README at the referenced
revision. Metadata is cached per host, repository, action subpath, and ref for
`cache.ttl`. A missing README or metadata fetch failure does not hide the other
hover content.

The LSP also offers **Update to {version} & pin to SHA** for an outdated ref at
the cursor. It pins the target selected by the update policy and per-action
overrides, even with `policy.pin = "tag"` or `"preserve"`. **Pin to commit SHA**
still pins the current version, including when it is up to date. Pin refactors
are available with the cursor anywhere in `owner/repo@ref`, including inside
`parallel:` steps; their edits replace only the ref and its applicable comment.
The update-and-pin refactor is omitted when the ordinary quick fix already makes
the identical edit; it remains available in a refactor-only request. Cached SHA
targets must be exactly 40 hexadecimal characters, and edits use current
document diagnostics.

On a line that takes no new comment, such as a line of a plain-text file, a
label comment right after the value is still rewritten. Writers read the word
after `#` as the label and the next word as the note, and leave the rest of the
line as written: `run("uses: o/p@<sha> # v4.0.0 keep this")` re-pinned becomes
`run("uses: o/p@<new> # v4.2.0 keep this")`. A word ends at whitespace, a quote,
a backslash, a bracket, `<`, `>`, `;` or `,`. After the only `uses:` value of a
plain-text line, the comment may also follow a closing quote and `}`, `]` or
`,`, as in `{"uses": "o/p@<sha>"},  # v4.0.0`.

Major tags must identify the selected release commit by default
(`policy.major_tag = "exact"`). If a major tag is ahead of the release or has
diverged, Actup reports a mismatch and offers no automatic rewrite. An ancestor
is outdated. If ancestry cannot be verified, the result is unknown and no
automatic rewrite is offered. This prevents a newer major tag from being
replaced by an older release commit, including SHA pins on that major tag.

For actions that publish an image from a release and then move their major tag
to a subsequent digest-pinning commit, opt into verified containment:

```toml
[[overrides]]
pattern = "kjanat/actionlint"
policy  = { major_tag = "contains" }
```

`contains` also accepts major tags whose commits descend from the selected
release. It does not accept divergent history or unverified ancestry, change
`track`, or relax `bump` restrictions. `track = "exact"` still selects the full
release; it never automatically downgrades a current major tag to its ancestor.
Comparisons use immutable commit SHAs and run only when needed. Successful
comparisons are cached per provider, host, repository and SHA pair with the
provider's existing retention policy. Failures and unsupported comparisons are
not cached. Providers without ancestry support return unknown.

Strict mismatches appear as warnings without fixes in the LSP. CLI check reports
them as an error with the mismatch reason (exit 3); MCP `getLatest` returns
`status: "unknown"`, `check: "mismatch"`, a reason, and no target. Explicit MCP
mutators retain their requested-target semantics.

A SHA pin whose comment starts with a fetched branch name tracks that branch:
`uses: owner/repo@<sha> # master` is outdated when `master` points at a
different commit. `update` and `pin` refresh the SHA, retaining the branch label
and any note under the default pin/comment settings. This also works inside
`parallel:` steps and for custom branch names. A matching head is a no-op. The
comment's branch takes precedence over release tags on the old commit; if a tag
and branch share the comment's name, the tag takes precedence. Unrecognized
comments and pins without comments keep the existing tag-based resolution.
`scan.ignore` still applies. The `policy.branch` setting controls floating
references such as `@master`, not these existing SHA pins. Cache freshness and
stale-write guards apply as usual; use `--refresh` to fetch current heads.

`actup pin --unpin` and the LSP refactor action `` actup: unpin to `v4` ``
rewrite `@<sha> # v4 note` to `@v4 # note`. They act only on a SHA pin whose
comment starts with a tag, and only when the fetched tags hold that tag on the
pinned commit. `pin --unpin` skips actions that `scan.ignore` matches. Neither
`update` nor fix-all unpins this way.

> [!WARNING]
> `pin = "tag"` unpins. It rewrites an outdated SHA pin to its target's tag,
> which the action's owner can move, and drops the label from its comment. A
> note after the label stays as the comment. Set `tag` only to leave SHA pins on
> purpose.

### Archived Repositories

The LSP asks the provider whether each action's repository is archived (GitHub,
GitLab, Gitea) or disabled (GitHub). It asks once per repository per
`cache.ttl`, and hover reuses the answer. An archived or disabled repository
gets a hint diagnostic with code `archived` on each `uses:` line and a warning
line in hover. A failed or rate-limited lookup reports nothing, and an action
that `scan.ignore` matches gets no lookup. `policy.archived = "ignore"` turns
both off, also per `[[overrides]]` entry.

### Config Discovery

1. `-c, --config <path>` (or `ACTUP_CONFIG`) of the CLI and `actup-mcp`, or LSP
   `configPath` (explicit). A relative path resolves against the working
   directory or the LSP workspace root. A blank `configPath` counts as unset. A
   missing file is an error (exit code 2).
2. Repo: `actup.toml`, `.actup.toml`, `.config/actup.toml`, searched from the
   scanned path upward. The search stops at the first directory that contains
   `.git` (a directory, or a file in a worktree). The LSP searches only its
   workspace folder, and `actup-mcp` only its `--root`.
3. User: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/actup/config.toml` on every OS when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
   is an absolute path, otherwise `actup/config.toml` in the OS config dir
   (`~/.config`, `~/Library/Application Support`, `%APPDATA%`)

A repo config arrives with the repository, so actup ignores the keys in it that
choose where a token goes, which files get rewritten or where cached SHAs come
from: `default_host`, `scan.extra_paths`, `hosts.<host>.api_base`,
`hosts.<host>.token_env` and `cache.path`. actup warns with the key and the
file, and `actup config` lists the ignored keys. A key that the explicit config
or an `ACTUP_*` variable also sets gets no warning and no listing. Set them in
the user config or in a file passed with `--config` or `configPath`. A
non-preset host that only the repo config declares gets no token.

The disk cache lives in `cache.path`, else in the OS cache dir
(`~/.cache/actup`, `~/Library/Caches/actup`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\actup\cache`). With
neither, the CLI, the LSP and `actup-mcp` warn once and run without a disk
cache, and `actup cache info` and `actup cache path` report that there is no
cache dir. `actup cache clear` deletes only the entry files actup writes and
keeps every other file in the directory.

An unknown key in a config file or in an `ACTUP_*` variable is an error (exit
code 2). The message names the file or the variable and suggests the closest
known key. A top-level `$schema` string, such as
`"$schema": "./schemas/actup-config.schema.json"`, is accepted in every format
and ignored. In a nested table, `$schema` is an unknown key.

The CLI and the LSP log every config source at `info`: the user file, the repo
file, the explicit file and the `ACTUP_*` variables that set config keys.
`actup config` lists the same sources from lowest to highest precedence, under
`sources` in JSON and TOML output.

### Environment Variables

**Authentication:**

- `GITHUB_TOKEN` - GitHub API authentication

**CLI defaults:**

- `ACTUP_CONFIG` - Config file path, same as `--config`
- `ACTUP_VERBOSE` - Enable verbose output
- `ACTUP_FORMAT` - Default `--format` of the subcommands (`human`, `json`,
  `toml`, and `table` or `sarif` for `check`); the quick lookup ignores it
- `ACTUP_STRICT` - Enable strict mode for `check`
- `ACTUP_COLOR` - Colour mode, same as `--color` (`auto`, `always`, `never`)

An empty value of one of these variables counts as unset.

**Config overrides:**

Every other `ACTUP_*` variable sets a config key over every config file. The
name after `ACTUP_` names the key path. `__` separates nesting levels, and a
single `_` stays part of a key name. Names match in any case. A value parses as
a boolean, number, array (`[..]`) or inline table (`{k = v}`), else as a string.

```sh
ACTUP_DEFAULT_HOST=github.com
ACTUP_POLICY__BUMP=patch
ACTUP_CACHE__TTL=3600
ACTUP_FETCH__MAX_TAGS_PER_REPO=20
ACTUP_SCAN__IGNORE='["my-org/*"]'
```

## Shell Completions

Shell is auto-detected from `$SHELL` if omitted:

```sh
# Auto-detect shell
actup completions >completions.sh

# Or specify explicitly
actup completions bash >~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/actup
actup completions zsh >~/.zfunc/_actup
actup completions fish >~/.config/fish/completions/actup.fish
actup completions powershell >>$PROFILE
```

## MCP Server

`actup-mcp` serves actup over the Model Context Protocol on stdio:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/kjanat/actup actup-mcp
```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "actup": { "command": "actup-mcp", "args": ["--root", "/path/to/repo"] }
  }
}
```

The server reads the user config and a repo config inside `--root` (default: its
working directory). Its config search stops at that root. `-c, --config <path>`
(or `ACTUP_CONFIG`) loads an explicit config file over the repo and user config.
An empty `ACTUP_CONFIG` counts as unset. A relative path resolves against the
working directory. A config that fails to load exits with code 2. The server
refuses every path outside the root, including symlinks that point out of it.
`getVersions` and `getLatest` read version sets through the disk cache that the
CLI and the LSP use. `updateFile` and `updateAllUsesToVersion` read no version
sets from that cache. `updateAllUsesToVersion` resolves `targetRef` from the
provider on every call, also when no ref matches, and fails on a host that no
provider serves. When `scan.ignore` matches every matching ref, it skips the
provider and lists those refs as skipped.

| Tool                     | Kind    | Purpose                                                 |
| ------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `actionGetReadme`        | read    | README of an action repository at a ref                 |
| `actionGetActionYml`     | read    | Raw and parsed `action.yml` at a ref                    |
| `getVersions`            | read    | Semver tags, latest tag, optionally branches            |
| `getLatest`              | read    | Version the policy (or `policyOverride`) moves a ref to |
| `updateFile`             | mutator | Replace refs of named `uses:` values in one file        |
| `updateAllUsesToVersion` | mutator | Move every reference to one action under a directory    |

Every result carries `provider`, `host` and `status` (`upToDate`, `outdated`,
`unknown`, `unresolvable`, `rateLimited`). Mutators accept `dryRun`, return each
change with its line, byte range, before and after text, a unified diff and a
reversal plan, and change nothing when called again with the same arguments.
They write like `update`: atomically, after a re-read that refuses a file whose
edited lines changed since the scan. `updateAllUsesToVersion` and `updateFile`
refuse an edited text that is not valid YAML or holds a different number of
`uses:` values. `updateFile` skips that check with `validateYaml: false`, and
refuses edits that name actions on more than one host. `updateAllUsesToVersion`
writes each ref in its `policy.pin` style, as `update` does. It lists each
matching `uses:` value that is not a valid reference under `unresolvable` with
its `error`, leaves it unchanged and reports status `unresolvable`. `updateFile`
replaces the ref of such a value when the rewritten value parses, and refuses a
value without `@`. A trailing label comment names a version or the current ref,
as in `@v4 # v4.0.0 note` or `@main # main note`. `updateFile` writes a new ref
that is a version token as a tag, and any other name except a SHA as a branch.
The label names the new ref when `updateFile` writes a tag over a tag or branch.
It drops the label when `updateFile` writes a branch, a SHA, or a tag over a SHA
pin. Each keeps the note, and any other comment stays. `getLatest` adds
`refKind` (`tag`, `branch` or `sha`) when the version list names `currentRef`,
and `sameCommit` (the target version) when the target sits on the commit that
`currentRef` already points at. `getVersions` and `getLatest` add `stale`,
shaped like the CLI field, when their versions come from an expired cache entry,
and the server answers the next call afresh.

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning                                                                                                         |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | Success / all up-to-date                                                                                        |
| 1    | A `check --fail-on` kind found, `update --dry-run` with changes, or `update`/`pin` skipped a ref it cannot edit |
| 2    | User error: unresolvable refs, invalid config, invalid CLI input                                                |
| 3    | Network/auth/rate-limit error, no provider for a ref's host, or stale data                                      |

## Files Scanned

- `.github/workflows/*.yml` / `.yaml`
- `action.yml` / `.yaml` and `.github/actions/*/action.yml` / `.yaml`
- Reusable workflows: `uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/foo.yml@ref`
- `scan.extra_paths` globs, relative to the scan root, and any file passed as
  the path argument. A directory that an entry matches, such as
  `.gitea/workflows`, expands to the `*.yml` and `*.yaml` files directly in it
  and to `*/action.yml` and `*/action.yaml` below it.

actup reads a file by its extension. It parses `.yml` and `.yaml` files as YAML,
and Markdown files (`.md`, `.markdown`) through their fenced `yaml` or `yml`
blocks. In every other file it reads `uses:` values that contain `@` line by
line. It never adds a version comment on such a line, rewrites only a label
comment right after the value as [Pin Style](#pin-style) describes, and checks
an edit there for an unchanged `uses:` count only.

actup rejects an `extra_paths` entry that is absolute or contains a `..`
segment. It skips any match that resolves outside the scan root through a
symlink. `update`, `pin` and the `actup-mcp` mutators refuse to write a file
that resolves outside the root.

files.examples/pin.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

if (($# < 1 || $# > 2)); then
	echo "usage: $0 <tag> [dir]" >&2
	exit 2
fi
tag="$1"
dir="${2:-$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/workflows}"
if [[ ! "${tag}" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
	echo "error: ${tag} is not a release tag like v1.2.3" >&2
	exit 2
fi
sha="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${tag}^{commit}")" || {
	echo "error: no tag ${tag} in this repository" >&2
	exit 1
}

for file in "${dir}"/*.yml; do
	sed -E -i.bak \
		-e "s|kjanat/actup@[^[:space:]]+ # v[^[:space:]]+|kjanat/actup@${sha} # ${tag}|" \
		-e "s|^([[:space:]]*version: )v[^[:space:]]+$|\\1${tag}|" \
		"${file}"
	rm -- "${file}.bak"
	echo "${file}: kjanat/actup@${sha} # ${tag}"
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -r -- "${work}"' EXIT

git_() {
	git -C "${work}/repo" -c user.name=actup -c user.email=actup@example.invalid \
		-c commit.gpgSign=false -c tag.gpgSign=false "$@"
}
mkdir -p "${work}/repo"
git_ init -q
git_ commit -q --allow-empty -m first
git_ tag v9.9.9
first="$(git_ rev-parse HEAD)"
git_ commit -q --allow-empty -m second
git_ tag v9.10.0-rc.1
second="$(git_ rev-parse HEAD)"

cp -R "${here}/workflows" "${work}/workflows"
examples=("${work}"/workflows/*.yml)
pin() { (cd "${work}/repo" && "${here}/pin.sh" "$@" "${work}/workflows") >"${work}/pin.log" 2>&1; }

failures=0
pass() { echo "ok - $1"; }
fail() {
	echo "not ok - $1"
	failures=$((failures + 1))
}

pins_everywhere() {
	local file
	for file in "${examples[@]}"; do
		grep -q "kjanat/actup@$1 # $2$" "${file}" && grep -q "version: $2$" "${file}" || return 1
	done
}

pin v9.9.9
if ! grep -rq "<release-sha>" "${work}/workflows" && pins_everywhere "${first}" v9.9.9; then
	pass "a tag replaces the placeholder, comment and version in every example"
else
	fail "a tag replaces the placeholder, comment and version in every example"
fi

other_pins() { grep -rh "actions/checkout@\|create-pull-request@" "$1" | sort; }
if diff <(other_pins "${here}/workflows") <(other_pins "${work}/workflows") >/dev/null; then
	pass "other pins stay as written"
else
	fail "other pins stay as written"
fi

pin v9.10.0-rc.1
if pins_everywhere "${second}" v9.10.0-rc.1 && ! grep -rq "${first}" "${work}/workflows"; then
	pass "a later tag replaces the earlier pin"
else
	fail "a later tag replaces the earlier pin"
fi

cp -R "${work}/workflows" "${work}/before"
status=0
pin latest || status=$?
if [[ "${status}" == 2 ]] && diff -r "${work}/before" "${work}/workflows" >/dev/null; then
	pass "a tag that is not a release tag is refused"
else
	fail "a tag that is not a release tag is refused"
fi

status=0
pin v1.2.3 || status=$?
if [[ "${status}" == 1 ]] && grep -q "no tag v1.2.3" "${work}/pin.log" \
	&& diff -r "${work}/before" "${work}/workflows" >/dev/null; then
	pass "a missing tag is refused"
else
	fail "a missing tag is refused"
fi

if ((failures > 0)); then
	echo "${failures} failed"
	exit 1
fi
echo "all passed"

set unstable := true

# Install

# Install all binaries to ~/.cargo/bin
[group('install')]
inst-all: install-actup install-actup-lsp install-actup-mcp

# Install actup CLI
[group('install')]
install-actup:
    cargo +stable install-actup

# Install actup-lsp language server
[group('install')]

    cargo +stable install-lsp

# Install actup-mcp server
[group('install')]

    cargo +stable install-mcp

# Uninstall binary from ~/.cargo/bin
[group('install')]
uninstall binary="actup":
    cargo uninstall {{ binary }}

# Build

# Build all packages (debug)
[group('build')]
build:
    cargo build --all

# Build all packages (release)
[group('build')]
build-release:
    cargo build --release --all

# Build only the CLI (release)
[group('build')]
cli:
    cargo build --package actup --release

# Check all packages compile
[group('build')]
check:
    cargo check --all

# Clean build artifacts
[group('build')]
clean:
    cargo clean

# Test

# Run all tests
[group('test')]
test:
    cargo test --all

# Run all tests with nextest
[group('test')]
nextest:
    cargo nextest run --all

# Run tests with output
[group('test')]
test-verbose:
    cargo test --all -- --nocapture

# Run tests for a specific package
[group('test')]
test-pkg pkg:
    cargo test --package {{ pkg }}

# Build actup-wasm for Node.js and run its crate node tests
[group('test')]

    wasm-pack build crates/wasm --target nodejs --out-dir ../../target/wasm-pkg
    node crates/wasm/tests/node_parse.mjs
    node crates/wasm/tests/node_check.mjs

# Test the GitHub Action install and run scripts
[group('test')]
action-test:
    shellcheck action/*.sh
    action/test.sh

# Test the crates.io publish script
[group('test')]
crates-publish-test:
    shellcheck .github/actions/crates-publish/*.sh
    .github/actions/crates-publish/test.sh

# Test the release version script
[group('test')]

    shellcheck .github/actions/release-version/*.sh
    .github/actions/release-version/test.sh

# Test the example-workflow pin script
[group('test')]

    examples/pin.test.sh

# Pin the example workflows to the commit of release tag `tag`
[group('docs')]

cov:

[group('test')]
cov-lcov:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --all --lcov --output-path {{ coverage-lcov }}

# Lint

# Run clippy on all packages
[group('lint')]
clippy:
    cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --workspace -- -D clippy::all

# Run all nightly lints
[env("RUSTFLAGS", "-Zmacro-backtrace")]
[group('lint')]
clippy-nightly:
    cargo +nightly clippy --all-targets --all-features --workspace -- -D clippy::all

# Run clippy strict (fail on warnings)
[group('lint')]
clippy-strict:
    cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

# Run clippy strict on actup-wasm for wasm32
[group('lint')]
clippy-wasm:
    cargo clippy -p actup-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings

# Format code
[group('lint')]
fmt:
    dprint fmt

# Check formatting without changes
[group('lint')]
fmt-check:
    dprint check

# Run all lints (fmt + clippy strict)
[group('lint')]
lint: fmt-check clippy clippy-strict clippy-wasm

# Run

# Run the CLI (debug build)
[group('run')]
run *args:
    cargo run --bin actup -- {{ args }}

# Run the CLI (release build)
[group('run')]
run-release *args:
    cargo run --bin actup --release -- {{ args }}

# Run actup binary directly
[group('run')]
actup *args:
    cargo run --bin actup -- {{ args }}

# Watch for changes and check
[group('run')]
watch:
    cargo watch -c -x check

# Cache

# Show cache info
[group('cache')]
cache-info:
    cargo run --bin actup -- cache info

# Clear the cache
[group('cache')]
cache-clear:
    cargo run --bin actup -- cache clear

# Print cache path
[group('cache')]
cache-path:
    @cargo run --bin actup -- cache path

# Docs

# Generate docs
[group('docs')]
doc:
    cargo doc --all --no-deps

# Generate and open docs
[group('docs')]
doc-open:
    cargo doc --all --no-deps --open

# Generate JSON schema for config
[group('docs')]
schema:
    @mkdir -p {{ schema_dir }}
    cargo run --bin actup -- schema > {{ config-schema }}

# Regenerate the `actup_core::yaml` simple uppercase table from a UnicodeData.txt 15.0.0 path
[group('docs')]
simple-upper ucd:
    cargo run --quiet -p actup-core --example gen_simple_upper -- {{ ucd }} crates/core/src/yaml/simple_upper.rs

# CI

# Run full CI checks locally
[group('ci')]
ci: fmt-check clippy-strict clippy-wasm test wasm-node-test action-test examples-test crates-publish-test release-version-test
    @echo "All CI checks passed!"

# Run actup on this repo
[group('ci')]
self-check:
    cargo run --release --package actup -- check

# Fail when a workflow or action ref in this repo is not pinned to a commit SHA
[group('ci')]
self-check-pins:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo run --package actup -- check --format json . \
        | jq -e 'map(select(.reference | test("^[0-9a-f]{40}$") | not)) | if length == 0 then true else map("\(.file):\(.line): \(.action) is not pinned to a commit SHA") | join("\n") + "\n" | halt_error(1) end'

# Run actup on this repo (verbose)
[group('ci')]
self-check-verbose:
    cargo run --release --package actup -- check --verbose

# Dependencies

# Update dependencies
[group('deps')]
update:
    cargo update

# Show outdated dependencies
[group('deps')]
outdated:
    cargo outdated -R

# Count lines of code
[group('deps')]
loc:
    @tokei crates/

# Extensions

# Check all editor extensions
[group('extensions')]
ext-check: zed::clippy vscode::lint vscode::typecheck vscode::test

# Verify the Rust→tsify→TS→consumer chain end-to-end (wasm build, wasm tests, then VS Code typecheck against fresh `.d.ts`)
[group('extensions')]
verify-wasm: wasm::build wasm::test vscode::typecheck

# Run full CI checks: ci, then wasm/TS shape verification, then extensions
[group('ci')]
ci-full: ci wasm::build wasm::test ext-check

# Branding

# Regenerate canonical icon PNGs from SVG sources (gitignored output, ad-hoc usage)
[group('branding')]
icons:
    bun branding/generate-icon.ts -s 128 -p 20 -r 18 "#0d1117" branding/icon.svg branding/icon-128.png
    bun branding/generate-icon.ts -s 256 -p 20 -r 36 "#0d1117" branding/icon.svg branding/icon-256.png
    bun branding/generate-icon.ts -s 512 -p 20 -r 72 "#0d1117" branding/icon.svg branding/icon-512.png
